children: The Bank of Japan kept its short-term policy rate unchanged at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote at its October meeting, meeting market expectations following consecutive 25-basis-point rate increases in June and September. The policy rate remains at its highest level since April 1995.

Policymakers signaled that further rate increases remain on the table, noting that underlying CPI inflation has aligned with the central bank's 2% target for the first time since its establishment in 2013.
The board highlighted that financial conditions remain accommodative, supported by persistent labor shortages and a moderate wage-price cycle.
Board member Hajime Takata dissented, advocating for faster rate increases toward the neutral rate given that inflation has reached target levels.
For FY2026 maintained the inflation forecast at 2.5% while raising the GDP growth projection to 0.7% (from 0.6%)
For FY2027 raised the inflation forecast to 2.6% (from 2.4%) while trimming the growth outlook to 0.7% (from 0.8%).
